mcq.q: Real GDP falls from ₹150 lakh crore in one quarter to ₹147 lakh crore in the next. The quarterly growth rate is:
mcq.explain: Growth rate = (147 − 150) ÷ 150 × 100 = −3 ÷ 150 × 100 = −2%. The negative sign shows that output is shrinking. Two successive quarters of falling real GDP are commonly used as a rough sign of a recession.
mcq.fast: Growth % = (new − old) ÷ old × 100; keep the sign.

mcq.q: An index of real output rises from 100 at a trough to 130 at the next peak and then falls to 117. The percentage fall from the peak is:
mcq.explain: Percentage fall = (130 − 117) ÷ 130 × 100 = 13 ÷ 130 × 100 = 10%. The base is the peak value, not the trough. Using the trough value as the base gives 13%, which is a common error.
mcq.fast: Measure a fall from the peak value (base = 130).

mcq.q: Which set of conditions best describes the peak of a business cycle?
options: Very high unemployment and widespread pessimism
Output and employment at their highest, input shortages and rising costs, with growth about to slow
Falling prices and large unsold stocks
Excess capacity and very low investment
mcq.explain: At the peak, the economy is operating at or near full capacity: output, employment and prices are high, input shortages appear and costs rise, so profit margins start to shrink. Growth then slows and the economy turns down. Unemployment, falling prices and excess capacity describe a contraction or trough.
mcq.fast: Peak = boom at its height: full capacity, shortages, rising costs.

mcq.q: Firms find unsold goods piling up in their warehouses, and orders begin to fall. This is typically the beginning of the:
mcq.explain: When demand stops keeping pace with output, firms accumulate unwanted inventories. They then reduce orders, cut production and postpone investment, which reduces employment and income. This marks the start of the contraction phase, which may deepen into a recession.
mcq.fast: Unwanted inventories + falling orders = contraction begins.

mcq.q: During the recovery phase after a trough, which of these usually happens first?
options: Prices rise sharply to their highest level
Firms begin replacing worn-out machinery and investment slowly picks up
mcq.explain: After a trough, depreciated machinery has to be replaced and interest rates are low, so investment gradually revives. This raises employment and income, and optimism slowly returns. Severe shortages, peak prices and minimum unemployment are features of the later boom, not of early recovery.
mcq.fast: Recovery starts with replacement investment.

mcq.q: A rise in building permits and in new orders for capital goods this quarter most likely signals:
options: A recession that has already ended
An expansion in economic activity in the coming months
mcq.explain: Building permits and new orders for capital goods are leading indicators: they change before the economy as a whole changes direction, because they reflect plans for future production and construction. Rising values therefore point to expanding activity ahead.
mcq.fast: Leading indicators look ahead; rising = expansion ahead.

mcq.q: Industrial production and personal income, which move at the same time as the overall economy, are:
mcq.explain: Coincident indicators change at roughly the same time as the economy as a whole, so they show the current state of the cycle. Examples are GDP, industrial production, personal income and retail sales. Leading indicators move earlier, and lagging indicators move later.
mcq.fast: Moves at the same time = coincident.

mcq.q: The bankruptcy of which US investment bank in September 2008 deepened the global financial crisis?
mcq.explain: Lehman Brothers, heavily exposed to US sub-prime mortgage securities, filed for bankruptcy in September 2008. Its collapse froze credit markets around the world and turned the US housing-related crisis into a global financial crisis and recession. The other banks survived the crisis.
mcq.fast: 2008 crisis symbol = Lehman Brothers collapse.

mcq.q: The Great Depression began with a crash of the stock market in:
mcq.explain: The Great Depression started after the Wall Street stock market crash of October 1929 in the United States and spread across the world in the 1930s, with huge falls in output, trade and prices and very high unemployment. It inspired Keynes's theory of effective demand.
mcq.fast: Great Depression = US, 1929.

mcq.q: The sharp fall in output in 2020 when governments imposed lockdowns to control COVID-19 is an example of a business cycle caused by:
options: An internal fluctuation in inventories only
mcq.explain: The 2020 downturn did not arise from the normal working of the economy; it was caused by a pandemic and the lockdowns imposed to control it, which are events outside the economic system. Such external or exogenous shocks — wars, pandemics, natural disasters — can trigger sharp contractions.
mcq.fast: Shock from outside the economy (pandemic, war, disaster) = external cause.

mcq.q: Which statement about business cycles is correct?
options: Every cycle lasts exactly the same number of years
They recur periodically, but their length and intensity are not uniform
They affect only the agricultural sector
They occur only in socialist economies
mcq.explain: Business cycles recur again and again, but they are not regular like clock-work: different cycles last different lengths of time and differ in severity. They are economy-wide, tend to spread from one sector and one country to others, and are a feature of market economies.
mcq.fast: Cycles: recurrent but irregular.

mcq.q: During a recession, which of these usually suffers the largest fall in demand?
options: Durable goods such as cars and machinery
mcq.explain: Purchases of durable consumer goods and capital goods can easily be postponed when incomes and confidence fall, so their demand falls the most in a downturn. Demand for necessities such as food, medicines and household electricity is relatively stable because people keep buying them anyway.
mcq.fast: Postponable purchases (durables, capital goods) swing most.

mcq.q: A manufacturer expects a recession next year. The most sensible step is to:
options: Build up large stocks of finished goods
Keep inventories lean and postpone non-essential expansion
Borrow heavily to double capacity immediately
mcq.explain: Understanding the business cycle helps firms plan. When a downturn is expected, demand is likely to fall, so firms should avoid piling up stocks, conserve cash and delay non-essential capacity expansion. Building inventories or borrowing heavily for expansion just before a recession increases risk.
mcq.topic: Relevance of business cycles in business decision making
mcq.fast: Downturn expected -> lean stocks, conserve cash.

mcq.q: A deep and prolonged contraction, with very high unemployment and falling prices, is called a:
mcq.explain: A depression is a severe and prolonged form of contraction: output and employment fall sharply, unemployment is very high, prices and wages fall, and business confidence is very low. The Great Depression of the 1930s is the classic example. A boom and peak are the opposite end of the cycle.
mcq.fast: Severe, long contraction = depression.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an internal (endogenous) cause of business cycles?
options: Fluctuations in investment spending by firms
mcq.explain: Internal causes arise within the economic system, such as fluctuations in investment, in effective demand, in money supply and bank credit, and changes in business expectations. Wars, natural disasters and pandemics come from outside the economy and are external causes.
mcq.fast: Inside the economy (investment, credit, expectations) = internal.

mcq.q: According to the monetary view of trade cycles, an expansion is started mainly by:
options: Banks expanding credit at low interest rates
mcq.explain: The monetary explanation (associated with Hawtrey) sees the trade cycle as a monetary phenomenon. When banks expand credit at low interest rates, traders borrow and buy more, production and income rise, and an expansion follows. When banks restrict credit, the process reverses into contraction.
mcq.fast: Monetary theory = bank credit drives the cycle.

mcq.q: Business cycles are best described as:
options: Fluctuations in aggregate economic activity around its long-term trend
Seasonal changes in the sale of umbrellas
Changes in the price of one good
mcq.explain: Business cycles are recurring ups and downs in overall economic activity — output, income, employment and prices — around the long-run growth trend. Seasonal changes in the sales of particular goods and changes in the price of one good are not business cycles, which affect the economy as a whole.
mcq.fast: Economy-wide ups and downs around the trend.

mcq.q: Unemployment that rises during a recession because of falling aggregate demand is called:
mcq.explain: Cyclical unemployment is caused by a fall in aggregate demand during the contraction phase of the business cycle, and it falls again during expansion. Frictional unemployment arises while workers move between jobs, seasonal unemployment follows seasons, and structural unemployment comes from long-term changes in the economy.
mcq.fast: Caused by the cycle = cyclical.

mcq.q: During the expansion phase of a business cycle, which of the following generally happens?
mcq.explain: In expansion, aggregate demand grows, firms increase production and investment, employment and incomes rise, and prices often start to rise as well. Rising unemployment, falling investment and falling prices are features of the contraction phase.
mcq.fast: Expansion = everything going up (output, jobs, income).

mcq.q: The bursting of the "dot-com bubble" at the start of the 2000s affected mainly the valuations of:
mcq.explain: In the late 1990s, share prices of internet-based and technology companies rose to very high levels on optimistic expectations. When the bubble burst around 2000–2001, these share prices collapsed, many such companies failed, and the US economy slipped into a mild recession.
mcq.fast: Dot-com = internet/tech shares.

mcq.q: Which business is most likely to see its demand hold up well even during a recession?
mcq.explain: Demand for basic necessities such as groceries is fairly stable whatever the state of the economy, because households must keep buying them. Luxury cars, holiday homes and capital goods are cyclical: buyers can postpone them, so their demand drops sharply in a recession.
mcq.topic: Relevance of business cycles in business decision making
mcq.fast: Necessities are defensive; postponable items are cyclical.

mcq.q: Business cycles are said to be "contagious" because:
options: A downturn in one sector or country tends to spread to others
mcq.explain: Because sectors and countries are linked through trade, finance and expectations, a slump in one major sector or economy tends to spread to others. For example, the 2008 US financial crisis spread to Europe and the rest of the world. This tendency to spread is described as the contagious nature of cycles.
mcq.fast: Contagious = spreads across sectors and countries.

mcq.q: The view that waves of optimism and pessimism among businessmen cause cycles links fluctuations mainly to:
mcq.explain: The psychological theory, associated with A. C. Pigou, holds that business expectations swing between optimism and pessimism. Optimism leads to over-investment and expansion; errors are then discovered, pessimism sets in and investment is cut too much, causing contraction. Expectations are therefore an internal cause.
mcq.fast: Optimism/pessimism = psychological (Pigou).

mcq.q: Share price indices are generally treated as a:
mcq.explain: Stock prices reflect investors' expectations of future profits, so they usually start rising before an economic recovery and falling before a downturn. That is why share price indices are treated as leading indicators. They are not part of national income.
mcq.fast: Stock markets look ahead -> leading.

mcq.q: Which phase of the business cycle immediately follows a trough?
mcq.explain: The trough is the lowest point of the cycle. After it, demand slowly revives, investment picks up and output and employment begin to rise — the recovery phase, which develops into expansion. The usual sequence is expansion, peak, contraction and trough, followed again by recovery.
mcq.fast: After the bottom comes recovery.

mcq.q: Knowledge of business cycles is useful to governments mainly because it helps them to:
options: Fix the prices of all goods
Design and time counter-cyclical fiscal and monetary policies
mcq.explain: Understanding where the economy stands in the cycle helps governments and central banks design and time stabilisation policies — for example, stimulating demand in a downturn and restraining it in an overheated boom. It does not mean controlling all prices or ending competition or trade.
mcq.topic: Relevance of business cycles in business decision making
mcq.fast: Cycle knowledge -> timely counter-cyclical policy.
